title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC equity — impose our persons for sinning, snatch them lest he be punished loco
pass_a_gloss: He laid our persons on Adam so Adam would sin loco nostro, and in the same moment took them off lest Adam also be punished loco nostro—as if God delighted in the death of us who had ourselves done no sin, and by that person-imposition sought nothing from Adam but a pretext to make us all sinners.
pass_b_english: He imposed our persons on him so that he might sin in our place, and at the same moment took them away lest he likewise be punished in our place.

It is as if he had delighted in the death of us ourselves, who had ourselves sinned nothing, and by that imposition of our persons on Adam had sought nothing else than an occasion of making us all sinners.
source_text: Nostras personas ei imposuerit ut peccaret loco nostro, ac eodem momento abstulerit ne puniretur itidem loco nostro: perinde ac si nostra ipsorum qui nihil ipsi peccaveramus, morte delectatus fuisset, nihilque aliud illa personarum nostrarum impositione Adamo captasset quam occasionem nos omnes efficiendi peccatores.

choices.choice: Persons on for sin, off before punishment; death-delight absurd
